questions.q: What is the general block form of a controlled-U gate (control=q1, target=q2)?
options: [[I, 0], [0, U]] — identity in the control=0 block, U in the control=1 block
[[U, 0], [0, I]] — U in the control=0 block, identity in the control=1 block
[[U, U], [U, U]] — U applied regardless of the control
[[I, I], [I, I]] — identity applied regardless of the control
questions.explain: Controlled-U does nothing when the control is |0⟩ (identity block) and applies U to the target when the control is |1⟩ (U block).

questions.q: What is CZ's explicit action on the basis states?
options: Flips the target qubit whenever the control is |1⟩
questions.explain: CZ is diag(1,1,1,-1): it's controlled-Z, and Z only affects the |1⟩ component, so only the |11⟩ term (both qubits |1⟩) picks up the sign flip.

questions.q: Why is CZ symmetric between its two qubits, unlike CNOT?
options: Because the condition 'both qubits are |1⟩' doesn't depend on which qubit is labeled the control
Because Z and X are the same gate
Because CZ doesn't actually depend on either qubit's state
It isn't symmetric — CZ behaves differently depending on which qubit is the control
questions.explain: Swapping which qubit is called the 'control' for CZ gives the exact same matrix, since the only state that gets flagged is |11⟩ regardless of labeling. CNOT has no such symmetry.

questions.q: When CZ is applied to the uniform superposition (|00⟩+|01⟩+|10⟩+|11⟩)/2, what is the result?
questions.explain: Direct computation shows only the |11⟩ amplitude flips sign, giving (|00⟩+|01⟩+|10⟩−|11⟩)/2 — the other three amplitudes are untouched.

questions.q: Why does the sign flip in the previous question count as a genuine relative phase rather than an irrelevant global phase?
options: It only flips the sign of one term in a superposition, not the entire state vector, which changes the state's physical behavior under later interference
It changes the measurement probabilities of all four outcomes
A relative phase and a global phase are the same thing physically
Because CZ is not a unitary gate
questions.explain: A global phase multiplies every amplitude equally and is unobservable. Here only the |11⟩ term's sign changes relative to the other three, which is measurable through interference even though it doesn't change these particular measurement probabilities.
